I fixed the bug I found in `wrap`, but I couldn't run the tests afterwards. Bash was denied partway through the session, so the fix and its new test are unverified.

You didn't say what was failing, and the existing 5 tests all passed before my change. So I probed the code and found one real bug. When the first word is longer than `width`, `wrap("abcdefghij a b", 5)` returned `['', 'abcdefghij', 'a b']`, with an empty string as the first line.

The fix is in `src/wrap.py`. The line-break check is now `if cur and len(cur) + extra > width:`, so it only starts a new line when there is already text on the current one. I added `test_wrap_long_first_word_no_empty_line` to `tests/test_wrap.py`. By my trace it should now return `['abcdefghij', 'a b']`.

If this wasn't the problem you meant, tell me what input or behavior looks wrong. To check the fix, run `python -m pytest -q` in the repo.
